import Mathlib

structure CycleGraph where
  adj : Array (Array Nat)

def CycleGraph.well_formed (g : CycleGraph) : Prop :=
  ∀ u, u < g.adj.size →
    ∀ v, v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[] → v < g.adj.size

def CycleGraph.size (g : CycleGraph) : Nat :=
  g.adj.size

def CycleGraph.has_edge (g : CycleGraph) (u v : Nat) : Prop :=
  u < g.adj.size ∧
  v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[]

def CycleGraph.is_path (g : CycleGraph) (p : List Nat) : Prop :=
  p.length > 0 ∧
  ∀ i, i + 1 < p.length →
    g.has_edge (p.getD i 0) (p.getD (i + 1) 0)

def CycleGraph.is_cycle (g : CycleGraph) (p : List Nat) : Prop :=
  g.is_path p ∧ p.length > 1 ∧ p.head? = p.getLast?

def CycleGraph.graph_has_cycle (g : CycleGraph) : Prop :=
  ∃ p, g.is_cycle p

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def has_cycle_precond (graph : CycleGraph) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  graph.well_formed
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- Successors of `u` as a list. -/
def cycAdj (g : CycleGraph) (u : Nat) : List Nat := (g.adj.getD u #[]).toList

/-- `cycLayer g k` is the list of nodes from which a walk with `k` edges starts.
    This is the "peeling" (Kahn-style) computation: layer `0` is every node, and a
    node survives to layer `k+1` exactly when one of its successors is in layer `k`.
    The layers shrink, so if a node survives `size` rounds the graph has a cycle. -/
def cycLayer (g : CycleGraph) : Nat → List Nat
  | 0 => List.range g.adj.size
  | k + 1 =>
      (List.range g.adj.size).filter
        (fun u => (cycAdj g u).any (fun v => decide (v ∈ cycLayer g k)))

/-- `hasWalk g k u` : there is a walk with `k` edges starting at `u`. -/
def hasWalk (g : CycleGraph) : Nat → Nat → Prop
  | 0, u => u < g.adj.size
  | k + 1, u => ∃ v, g.has_edge u v ∧ hasWalk g k v
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def has_cycle (graph : CycleGraph)
    (h_precond : has_cycle_precond graph) : Bool :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  !(cycLayer graph graph.adj.size).isEmpty
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def has_cycle_postcond (graph : CycleGraph) (result : Bool)
    (_ : has_cycle_precond graph) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  result = graph.graph_has_cycle
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem cyc_mem_adj (g : CycleGraph) (u v : Nat) :
    v ∈ cycAdj g u ↔ v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[] := by
  simp [cycAdj]

theorem cyc_layer_iff (g : CycleGraph) : ∀ k u, u ∈ cycLayer g k ↔ hasWalk g k u := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero => intro u; simp [cycLayer, hasWalk]
  | succ k ih =>
    intro u
    constructor
    · intro h
      rw [cycLayer, List.mem_filter] at h
      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := h
      rw [List.any_eq_true] at h2
      obtain ⟨v, hv, hv2⟩ := h2
      simp only [hasWalk]
      refine ⟨v, ⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
      · simpa using h1
      · exact (cyc_mem_adj g u v).1 hv
      · exact (ih v).1 (of_decide_eq_true hv2)
    · intro h
      simp only [hasWalk] at h
      obtain ⟨v, he, hw⟩ := h
      rw [cycLayer, List.mem_filter]
      refine ⟨by simpa using he.1, ?_⟩
      rw [List.any_eq_true]
      exact ⟨v, (cyc_mem_adj g u v).2 he.2, decide_eq_true ((ih v).2 hw)⟩

theorem hasWalk_mono (g : CycleGraph) :
    ∀ k j u, j ≤ k → hasWalk g k u → hasWalk g j u := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro j u hj h
    obtain rfl : j = 0 := Nat.le_zero.1 hj
    exact h
  | succ k ih =>
    intro j u hj h
    simp only [hasWalk] at h
    obtain ⟨v, he, hw⟩ := h
    cases j with
    | zero => exact he.1
    | succ j =>
      simp only [hasWalk]
      exact ⟨v, he, ih j v (by omega) hw⟩

theorem hasWalk_of_inf (g : CycleGraph) (f : Nat → Nat)
    (hf : ∀ t, g.has_edge (f t) (f (t + 1))) : ∀ k s, hasWalk g k (f s) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero => intro s; exact (hf s).1
  | succ k ih =>
    intro s
    simp only [hasWalk]
    exact ⟨f (s + 1), hf s, ih (s + 1)⟩

theorem walkFn_of_hasWalk (g : CycleGraph) : ∀ k u, hasWalk g k u →
    ∃ f : Nat → Nat, f 0 = u ∧ ∀ s, s < k → g.has_edge (f s) (f (s + 1)) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro u _
    exact ⟨fun _ => u, rfl, by intro s hs; omega⟩
  | succ k ih =>
    intro u h
    simp only [hasWalk] at h
    obtain ⟨v, he, hw⟩ := h
    obtain ⟨f, hf0, hf⟩ := ih v hw
    refine ⟨fun s => if s = 0 then u else f (s - 1), by simp, ?_⟩
    intro s hs
    cases s with
    | zero => simpa [hf0] using he
    | succ s => simpa using hf s (by omega)

theorem getD_range_map (h : Nat → Nat) (m i : Nat) (hi : i < m) :
    ((List.range m).map h).getD i 0 = h i := by
  have hlen : i < ((List.range m).map h).length := by simp [hi]
  rw [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hlen]
  simp

theorem cycle_of_repeat (g : CycleGraph) (f : Nat → Nat) (a b : Nat)
    (hab : a < b) (hbn : b ≤ g.adj.size)
    (hf : ∀ s, s < g.adj.size → g.has_edge (f s) (f (s + 1)))
    (heq : f a = f b) : g.graph_has_cycle := by
  refine ⟨(List.range (b - a + 1)).map (fun t => f (a + t)), ⟨by simp, ?_⟩, by simp; omega, ?_⟩
  · intro i hi
    have hlen : ((List.range (b - a + 1)).map (fun t => f (a + t))).length = b - a + 1 := by
      simp
    rw [hlen] at hi
    rw [getD_range_map _ _ i (by omega), getD_range_map _ _ (i + 1) (by omega)]
    have : a + (i + 1) = (a + i) + 1 := by omega
    rw [this]
    exact hf (a + i) (by omega)
  · have h0 : 0 < ((List.range (b - a + 1)).map (fun t => f (a + t))).length := by simp
    have hm : b - a < ((List.range (b - a + 1)).map (fun t => f (a + t))).length := by
      simp
    rw [List.head?_eq_getElem?, List.getLast?_eq_getElem?,
      List.getElem?_eq_getElem h0]
    have hidx : ((List.range (b - a + 1)).map (fun t => f (a + t))).length - 1 = b - a := by
      simp
    rw [hidx, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hm]
    simp only [List.getElem_map, List.getElem_range, Option.some_inj]
    have hb : a + (b - a) = b := by omega
    rw [hb]
    simpa using heq

theorem cycle_of_hasWalk (g : CycleGraph) (hwf : g.well_formed) (u : Nat)
    (h : hasWalk g g.adj.size u) : g.graph_has_cycle := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf0, hf⟩ := walkFn_of_hasWalk g g.adj.size u h
  have hun : u < g.adj.size := hasWalk_mono g g.adj.size 0 u (Nat.zero_le _) h
  have hbound : ∀ s, s ≤ g.adj.size → f s < g.adj.size := by
    intro s hs
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge s g.adj.size with hlt | hge
    · exact (hf s hlt).1
    · have hsn : s = g.adj.size := by omega
      have he := hf (g.adj.size - 1) (by omega)
      have hsucc : g.adj.size - 1 + 1 = g.adj.size := by omega
      rw [hsucc] at he
      rw [hsn]
      exact hwf (f (g.adj.size - 1)) he.1 (f g.adj.size) he.2
  set F : Fin (g.adj.size + 1) → Fin g.adj.size :=
    fun i => ⟨f i.val, hbound i.val (Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp i.isLt)⟩ with hF
  have hni : ¬ Function.Injective F := by
    intro hinj
    have hcard := Fintype.card_le_of_injective F hinj
    rw [Fintype.card_fin, Fintype.card_fin] at hcard
    omega
  obtain ⟨x, y, hxy, hne⟩ := Function.not_injective_iff.mp hni
  have hval : f x.val = f y.val := congrArg Fin.val hxy
  have hxn : x.val ≤ g.adj.size := Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp x.isLt
  have hyn : y.val ≤ g.adj.size := Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp y.isLt
  have hnev : x.val ≠ y.val := fun hc => hne (Fin.ext hc)
  rcases Nat.lt_or_ge x.val y.val with hlt | hge
  · exact cycle_of_repeat g f x.val y.val hlt hyn hf hval
  · have hlt' : y.val < x.val := by omega
    exact cycle_of_repeat g f y.val x.val hlt' hxn hf hval.symm

theorem inf_of_cycle (g : CycleGraph) (p : List Nat) (hc : g.is_cycle p) :
    ∃ f : Nat → Nat, ∀ t, g.has_edge (f t) (f (t + 1)) := by
  obtain ⟨⟨hpos, hstep⟩, hlen, hhl⟩ := hc
  set m := p.length - 1 with hm
  have hmpos : 0 < m := by omega
  have h0 : 0 < p.length := by omega
  have hml : m < p.length := by omega
  have hlast : p.getD m 0 = p.getD 0 0 := by
    have hh := hhl
    rw [List.head?_eq_getElem?, List.getLast?_eq_getElem?, ← hm,
      List.getElem?_eq_getElem h0, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hml] at hh
    rw [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD,
      List.getElem?_eq_getElem hml, List.getElem?_eq_getElem h0]
    simp only [Option.getD_some, Option.some_inj] at hh ⊢
    exact hh.symm
  refine ⟨fun s => p.getD (s % m) 0, ?_⟩
  intro t
  have hr : t % m < m := Nat.mod_lt _ hmpos
  by_cases hcase : t % m + 1 < m
  · have hmod : (t + 1) % m = t % m + 1 := by
      rw [Nat.add_mod, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (show 1 < m by omega), Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (by omega)]
    simp only [hmod]
    exact hstep (t % m) (by omega)
  · have hcase' : t % m + 1 = m := by omega
    have hmod : (t + 1) % m = 0 := by
      rcases Nat.lt_or_ge 1 m with h1 | h1
      · rw [Nat.add_mod, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt h1, hcase', Nat.mod_self]
      · have hm1 : m = 1 := by omega
        rw [hm1]
        omega
    simp only [hmod]
    have hs := hstep (t % m) (by omega)
    rw [hcase', hlast] at hs
    exact hs
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem has_cycle_postcond_satisfied (graph : CycleGraph)
    (h_precond : has_cycle_precond graph) :
    has_cycle_postcond graph (has_cycle graph h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  simp only [has_cycle_postcond]
  apply propext
  constructor
  · intro h
    simp only [has_cycle] at h
    obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ : ∃ u, u ∈ cycLayer graph graph.adj.size := by
      rcases hnil : cycLayer graph graph.adj.size with _ | ⟨x, t⟩
      · rw [hnil] at h; simp at h
      · exact ⟨x, by simp⟩
    exact cycle_of_hasWalk graph h_precond u ((cyc_layer_iff graph _ u).1 hu)
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨p, hc⟩ := h
    obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := inf_of_cycle graph p hc
    have hmem : f 0 ∈ cycLayer graph graph.adj.size :=
      (cyc_layer_iff graph _ (f 0)).2 (hasWalk_of_inf graph f hf _ 0)
    simp only [has_cycle]
    rcases hnil : cycLayer graph graph.adj.size with _ | ⟨x, t⟩
    · rw [hnil] at hmem; simp at hmem
    · simp
  -- !benchmark @end proof

## What was implemented

**Algorithm** (`has_cycle`, in the `code` marker): `!(cycLayer graph graph.adj.size).isEmpty`.

`cycLayer` (auxcode) is a Kahn-style peeling computation over the adjacency list:
- layer `0` = all nodes (`List.range n`),
- layer `k+1` = nodes having some successor in layer `k`.

So layer `k` is exactly the set of nodes from which a walk with `k` edges starts. The layers shrink monotonically, so a node surviving `n = size` rounds forces a repeated vertex among the `n+1` visited nodes — i.e. a cycle. It terminates structurally (fixed number of rounds), no visited-set recursion needed, and it's a real graph computation, not enumeration of candidate cycles or a decidability oracle over the postcondition.

**Proof chain** (lemma section):
- `cyc_layer_iff`: `u ∈ cycLayer g k ↔ hasWalk g k u` (the executable layers match the walk predicate).
- `walkFn_of_hasWalk` + `cycle_of_hasWalk`: from a walk with `n` edges, build `f : ℕ → ℕ` along it, bound `f s < n` for `s ≤ n` (the last node needs `well_formed` — this is where the precondition is used), then pigeonhole `Fin (n+1) → Fin n` via non-injectivity, and `cycle_of_repeat` builds the explicit cycle list `(List.range (b-a+1)).map (f ∘ (a + ·))` and discharges `is_path`, `length > 1`, `head? = getLast?`.
- `inf_of_cycle` + `hasWalk_of_inf`: from a cycle `p`, the periodic map `s ↦ p.getD (s % (p.length-1)) 0` is an infinite walk (wrap-around case uses `head? = getLast?`), giving walks of every length, hence a nonempty layer `n`.

The postcondition is proved as a genuine `propext` of both directions of `result = true ↔ graph.graph_has_cycle`.

## Semantic audit
- Markers all preserved; only `auxcode`, `code`, `lemma`, `proof` edited; no `sorry`/`admit`/axioms/`partial`/`unsafe`.
- Precondition `well_formed` is genuinely used (bounding the final vertex of the walk); the postcondition is unchanged and proved in full, both soundness and completeness.
- Edge cases: `size = 0` → layer 0 is `[]` → returns `false`, correct since `has_edge` is unsatisfiable. Self-loop `#[#[0]]` → returns `true`, matching the cycle `[0,0]` (length 2 > 1). Acyclic `#[#[1], #[]]` → layer 2 empty → `false`. No helper is a stub (`hasWalk`, `cycAdj`, `cycLayer` all carry real content).
